answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities the way an orchard resists a bad season: trust must be grown, not claimed. A new agent starts at the nadir of reputation — near-zero spending power and no voting weight — and earns standing only through sustained, attested work. Tending a tundra research post through winter takes real effort, so an attacker who spawns a thousand fresh identities must pay the full cost of real work for each one. Sybil identities stay cheap to create but worthless to use, which breaks the attack economics.
